Willis won the Democratic primary in her bid for reelection as Fulton County District Attorney in May 2024, defeating progressive attorney Christian Wise Smith and setting up a general election contest against Republican [[courtney-kramer|Courtney Kramer]] in the fall.[{n}] After the victory she told reporters that voters had sent a message that 'people want a DA that is just, that treats everybody equally and that works hard, and they know that they have that in me.'[{n}] Her public profile had been boosted by the [[state-of-georgia-v-trump|Trump election interference case]] and by racketeering cases against well-known rappers, though on election night she emphasized her record against violent crime and gang members alongside second-chance programs for first offenders and interventions for at-risk youth.[{n}] Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] noted that her race was called within about 30 minutes and that, unlike Judge [[scott-mcafee|Scott McAfee]], her electability remained an open question heading into the fall.[{n}]

McAfee, the Fulton County Superior Court judge randomly assigned to preside over the Georgia election interference case, fended off a challenger in May 2024, winning a nonpartisan election to keep his seat.[{n}] Badlands contributor [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] stressed that McAfee had not been in a primary but in the definitive contest, and would serve a full four-year term beginning in January 2025 — meaning Georgia voters had decisively chosen for him to continue judging, his most high-profile assignment being [[fani-willis|Fani Willis]]'s case against [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]].[{n}] She recalled that McAfee had ruled Willis could only continue the case if special prosecutor [[nathan-wade|Nathan Wade]] stepped aside; Wade promptly left, but a defense appeal of the ruling was pending before the Georgia Court of Appeals.[{n}] During the campaign, critics had claimed McAfee's notoriety hurt his electability and that electability pressures might compromise his impartiality — concerns Ashe deemed moot after the win.[{n}] She also noted that the Atlanta Journal-Constitution devoted barely two paragraphs to McAfee's victory while concentrating on Willis's primary.[{n}]
Departure from the Georgia case and 2024 appeal

Judge [[scott-mcafee|Scott McAfee]] ruled that [[fani-willis|Fani Willis]] could only continue the Georgia election interference case if special prosecutor Wade stepped aside; Wade promptly left the case.[{n}] As of May 2024, a defense appeal of McAfee's ruling was pending before the Georgia Court of Appeals.[{n}]
May 2024 primary results for the case's principals

In May 2024, both principals in the Georgia case prevailed at the ballot box: District Attorney [[fani-willis|Fani Willis]] won the Democratic primary against progressive attorney Christian Wise Smith, and Judge [[scott-mcafee|Scott McAfee]] won a nonpartisan election for a full four-year term beginning in January 2025.[{n}] Willis was set to face Republican [[courtney-kramer|Courtney Kramer]] in the fall general election.[{n}] The sprawling racketeering case against [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] and others had substantially raised Willis's public profile, and a defense appeal of McAfee's ruling forcing special prosecutor [[nathan-wade|Nathan Wade]] off the case remained pending before the Georgia Court of Appeals.[{n}]
Protecting Americans in the IDF Act (2024)

In May 2024, Miller co-introduced the [[protecting-americans-in-the-idf-act|Protecting Americans in the IDF Act]] with Representative [[guy-reschenthaler|Guy Reschenthaler]], legislation that would extend U.S. uniformed-service employment protections to Americans serving in the [[israel-defense-forces|Israeli Defense Forces]].[{n}] Miller said that 'as our closest ally in the Middle East continues to defend itself against terror, many brave Americans have decided to lend a hand,' and that he was proud the legislation extended important protections to Americans who chose to risk their lives in the fight against terror.[{n}]
American volunteers and the 2024 IDF benefits bill

In May 2024, Representatives [[guy-reschenthaler|Guy Reschenthaler]] and [[max-miller|Max Miller]] introduced the [[protecting-americans-in-the-idf-act|Protecting Americans in the IDF Act]], which would treat service by U.S. citizens in the IDF the same as service in the U.S. uniformed services for purposes of employment and financial protections.[{n}] Reschenthaler stated that over 20,000 American citizens were then defending Israel from Hamas.[{n}] Critics, including Badlands contributor [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]], questioned whether the bill was intended to encourage U.S. citizens with Israeli dual citizenship to enlist, and whether it conflicted with U.S. Code § 2387 on activities affecting the armed forces.[{n}]
